step1_figure.circuit_type: AC-coupled, self-biased cascode amplifier with source follower output
step1_figure.description: The netlist implements a high-gain cascode amplifier followed by a PMOS source follower buffer. The biasing network (100k Rs, 1uF Cbig, 1G Rbig) exactly matches the AC-coupled, self-biased testbench setup shown in Fig 21.21, which is used to evaluate amplifier frequency response and pole splitting.

equation.explanation: Total input-referred noise PSD based on the noise currents of the amplifying and load devices.
equation.assumptions: Thermal noise dominates, 1/f noise ignored in this specific expression.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming ID=20uA, W/L=10. gmn=328uS, gmp=141uS. I_M^2 = 4kT*gamma*gm. Vinoise^2 = 4kT*gamma*(gm1+gm2)/gm1^2 = 1.1e-20 * 469u / 1.07e-7 = 4.8e-17 V^2/Hz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on actual bias current and device sizing.

source_follower_gain.description: Small-signal voltage gain of the source follower stage

equation.explanation: Voltage divider between the source resistance of the amplifying device and the load.
equation.assumptions: Body effect is neglected or lumped into gm.

sky130_expected.calculation: With an active current source load, Rload = ro = 500k. 1/gmp = 7.1k. Av = 500k / (500k + 7.1k) = 0.986 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Source followers with active loads have gain very close to 1.

source_follower_rout.description: Output resistance of the source follower

equation.explanation: Parallel combination of the resistances looking into the source of M2 and drain of M1.
equation.assumptions: Ideal current source load simplifies this to ~1/gm.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by 1/gm of the PMOS source follower.

cg_input_resistance.description: Input resistance of a common-gate amplifier

equation.explanation: Resistance looking into the source of the common-gate device.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard 1/gm value for typical bias currents.

cg_gain.description: Voltage gain of a common-gate amplifier

equation.explanation: Ratio of transconductances of the amplifying device and the diode-connected load.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming W1/L1 = W2/L2. Av = sqrt(270u / 50u) = 2.32 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the mobility ratio between NMOS and PMOS.

slew_rate.description: Maximum rate of change of the output voltage

equation.explanation: Determined by the maximum current available to charge/discharge the load capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Class A operation, limited by the bias current source.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming I = 20uA and C_L = 1pF. SR = 20uA / 1pF = 20 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Directly proportional to bias current and inversely to load cap.

cs_small_signal_gain.description: Small-signal voltage gain of the common-source amplifier

equation.explanation: Transconductance multiplied by the total output resistance at the drain node.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical intrinsic gain for a single stage in 130nm.

open_circuit_gain.description: Maximum possible gain of a single MOSFET

equation.explanation: Gain when the load is an ideal current source (infinite resistance).

sky130_expected.reasoning: Intrinsic gain limit of the technology.

input_pole.description: Frequency of the pole at the input node

equation.explanation: RC pole formed by the source resistance and the Miller-multiplied input capacitance.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by the large 100k Rs and Miller capacitance.

output_pole.description: Frequency of the pole at the output node

equation.explanation: RC pole formed by the output resistance and output capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Before pole splitting effects are considered.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Output node has high resistance but low capacitance.

equation.explanation: Zero caused by feedforward current through the gate-drain capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Cgd is the dominant feedforward path.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Very high frequency due to small Cgd.

equation.explanation: Full magnitude transfer function including two poles and one zero.

sky130_expected.calculation: Evaluated across frequency in AC sweep.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Frequency dependent.

equation.explanation: Phase response including the inverting DC gain (180 deg) and phase drops from poles and RHP zero.

sky130_expected.calculation: Evaluated across frequency in AC sweep.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Frequency dependent.

cin_miller.description: Effective input capacitance due to Miller effect

equation.explanation: Input capacitance is magnified by the voltage gain across Cgd.
equation.assumptions: Gain is constant at low frequencies.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by Miller multiplication of Cgd.

cout_miller.description: Effective output capacitance due to Miller effect

equation.explanation: Output capacitance contribution from the Miller capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Gain is large, so 1/|Av| is small.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Miller effect on output side is minimal.

pole1_splitting.description: Dominant low-frequency pole with pole splitting

equation.explanation: The dominant pole moves to a lower frequency due to the increased effective Miller capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Cgd1*(1+|Av|) is much larger than other capacitances.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Pushed down by the large Rs and Miller cap.

pole2_splitting.description: Non-dominant high-frequency pole with pole splitting

equation.explanation: The second pole moves to a higher frequency as the gain decreases, breaking the Miller effect.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Pushed to high frequencies by pole splitting.

generic_zero.description: Zero location in generic compensated amplifier

equation.explanation: RHP zero caused by the compensation capacitor Cc.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the explicit compensation capacitor size.

generic_pole1.description: Dominant pole in generic compensated amplifier

equation.explanation: Dominant pole set by the Miller-multiplied compensation capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Large gain in the second stage.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Very low frequency due to large gain and Cc.

generic_pole2.description: Non-dominant pole in generic compensated amplifier

equation.explanation: Second pole location after pole splitting by Cc.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Pushed very high by large Cc.

generic_adc.description: DC gain of generic two-stage amplifier

equation.explanation: Product of the gains of the two stages.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical two-stage gain.

equation.explanation: Same as the dominant pole f1.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches f1.

unity_gain_freq.description: Unity gain frequency of the amplifier

equation.explanation: Frequency where the open-loop gain crosses 0 dB.
equation.assumptions: f_un is much larger than f3dB and single-pole roll-off dominates.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by input transconductance and compensation/load capacitance.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC open-loop gain, bandwidth, unity gain frequency, phase margin, and transient response of the AC-coupled cascode amplifier.
